method.warmup_policy: 1 discarded generation (manifest p1, same 512 cap) per block, EQUAL on both sides
method.rtf_definition: generation_wall_s / audio_duration_s (audio = len(waveform)/sr of the returned full utterance)

memory_measurement.in_process: torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated, reset right after model load (qwen side: the whole single process; vllm side: ONLY the orchestrator process - workers are spawned separately)
memory_measurement.whole_stack: 1 Hz polling of /sys/class/drm/card1/device/mem_info_vram_used + mem_info_gtt_used (amdgpu driver counters), identical sampler on both sides; peaks per phase (load/warmup/measured); rocm-smi snapshots wrap every block in the transcript. NOTE on this gfx1151 unified-memory APU the VRAM carveout counter stays flat (~1.34 GB, desktop) - stack allocations land in the GTT counter, so the informative whole-stack figure is the GTT peak (or vram+gtt sum), reported per side

method.env_isolation: separate venvs (.venv vs .work-vllm/venv), separate processes per block (full unload between blocks, verified by sysfs/rocm-smi snapshots in the transcript); qwen side runs WITHOUT HF_HOME set, vllm side with HF_HOME=.work-vllm/hf-home HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
method.batch_concurrency: not exercised in the tested path - both APIs nominally accept batched inputs (qwen_tts: List[str] text; end2end.py: --batch-size/--use-batch-sample), but this A/B measures per-prompt RTF parity at batch=1 (the documented default single-sample invocation); batch throughput parity is out of scope and listed unproven

fairness_notes: max_new_tokens=512 is an explicit official-API cap on the qwen side (generate_custom_voice(max_new_tokens=512)). The vLLM-Omni side carries "max_new_tokens": [512] inside additional_information exactly as end2end.py does, BUT code inspection of vllm-omni 0.28.0 shows the qwen3_tts offline pipeline does not consume that field (generation terminates on the talker stop token 2150 / EOS under engine-default sampling). Effective token-cap equivalence therefore does NOT hold by knob; it holds in practice for this workload because no tested prompt reaches either cap (longest output <=~20 s audio ~=<=240 tokens at 12 Hz < 512), so neither side was truncated.

Sampling params: neither side passes overrides. qwen side = checkpoint generate_config.json defaults (do_sample=true, temperature=0.9, top_k=50, top_p=1.0, repetition_penalty=1.05). vllm side = vllm-omni engine defaults (per-request sampling is not part of the end2end.py CustomVoice invocation pattern). Outputs are therefore not expected to be identical samples; the comparison is timing/memory, not sample equality (deterministic-vs-sampled equality was never claimed).
Both sides load the SAME checkpoint directory models/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice (qwen: loader.resolve_path; vllm: HF_HOME hub snapshot symlink to it).
instruct="" (blank) on both sides: both stacks treat a blank instruct as absent (verified in qwen_tts processing and vllm-omni prompt_embeds_builder: `if instruct.strip()`).
vllm wall times include its full per-request pipeline (talker prefill + decode + Code2Wav codec->wav), mirroring the qwen side's single official API call covering the same end-to-end span.
unsupported_parity: per-request sampling control on the vLLM-Omni offline path (no knob in the end2end.py CustomVoice pattern)
effective per-request token cap on the vLLM-Omni offline path (additional_information max_new_tokens not consumed by the qwen3_tts pipeline in 0.28.0)
batch/throughput comparison (supported by both APIs, not exercised here)
output-quality comparison (explicitly out of scope; Task 14 builds quality metrics)
